title: Letter to the Editor: Elbridge Colby’s Criticism of 1990s U.S. Policy
gist: A rebuttal letter from Richard E. Feinberg, Clinton’s senior director for Inter-American Affairs at the NSC, to Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby’s July 29 attack on 1990s U.S. Latin America policy. The core point is institutional: Colby’s own showcase venue — the 17th Conference of Defense Ministers of the Americas in Cusco — was created by the Clinton administration in 1995, as were the Summit of the Americas and the FTAA push, meaning the current hemispheric turn runs on architecture it disparages.

insights.claim: Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby publicly attacked the Clinton administration’s Latin America policy on July 29, 2026 as “highly aspirational abstractions,” “liberal internationalism,” and a “Peace Corps vision,” drawing a direct rebuttal from the era’s NSC senior director for Inter-American Affairs.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: The current administration is publicly framing its hemispheric doctrine as a break with the 1990s, which signals a willingness to discard existing multilateral machinery rather than inherit it.
insights.quote: “highly aspirational abstractions,” “liberal internationalism,” and “Peace Corps vision of American policy toward Latin America.”
insights.locator: In his Americas Quarterly article published on July 29

insights.claim: The 17th Conference of Defense Ministers of the Americas in Cusco, Peru — the forum where Colby made his case — was itself created by the Clinton administration in 1995 as a follow-up to the Miami Summit of the Americas.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
entities: Conference of Defense Ministers of the Americas
insights.so_what: The Trump-era hemispheric pivot operates through 1990s-built institutions; the continuity of the plumbing matters more than the rhetorical rupture when forecasting actual regional security cooperation.
insights.quote: a forum we initiated in 1995, as a follow-up to the Miami Summit of the Americas
insights.locator: Ironically, Colby was reporting on his participation

insights.claim: The letter closes by attributing Colby’s refusal to credit predecessors to the political culture of serving under Donald Trump, framing the dispute as partisan rather than analytical.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Expect continued open friction between the incumbent foreign policy team and the bipartisan hemispheric establishment — reduces the odds of durable, cross-administration commitments in the region.
insights.quote: Alas, such generosity would not be characteristic of those who serve at the pleasure of President Donald Trump.

themes.theme: Design logic of the defense ministerials

insights.claim: The 1995 defense ministerial architecture was deliberately built to keep U.S. and regional military officers low-profile while civilian democratic rule was consolidating, because visible military presence was judged to muddy the waters.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
entities: Conference of Defense Ministers of the Americas
insights.so_what: A reusable design principle for hemispheric security policy: the legitimacy cost of visible U.S. military engagement is a first-order constraint, one the current militarized framing appears to discount.
insights.quote: we were focused on the consolidation of civilian democratic rule and felt that a visible presence of U.S. and regional military officers could muddy the waters

insights.claim: The original mandate for hemispheric defense establishments was already organized crime, international terrorism and border confidence-building — the same agenda now presented as a new departure.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
entities: Conference of Defense Ministers of the Americas
insights.so_what: Claims of a doctrinal 'fundamental change' in hemispheric security should be discounted; the substantive agenda has been stable for three decades, so what changes is intensity and unilateralism, not focus.
insights.quote: the hemisphere’s defense establishments had important roles to play in supporting civil institutions, combatting organized crime and international terrorism

themes.theme: Trade architecture and the global-versus-regional tussle

insights.claim: The Clinton administration launched the Summit of the Americas and the Free Trade Area of the Americas over the objections of globalists inside its own government, and passed NAFTA (initiated by George H.W. Bush) — evidence that regional prioritization is a recurring, bipartisan U.S. impulse rather than a Trump-era invention.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
entities: Free Trade Area of the Americas
insights.so_what: Hemispheric-first trade policy has deep bipartisan roots, which raises the persistence odds of the current Western Hemisphere focus beyond one administration.
insights.quote: over the objections of many of the globalists in the government
insights.locator: But it was the Clinton administration that initiated

insights.claim: U.S. foreign policy is framed as a permanent tussle between the general and the particular, the global and the regional — a cyclical oscillation, not a one-way doctrinal shift.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Treat the current Western Hemisphere emphasis as a phase in an oscillation; positioning that assumes permanence in regional attention carries mean-reversion risk.
insights.quote: U.S. foreign policy is always a tussle between the general and the particular, the global and the regional.
insights.locator: Colby also asserts that we failed to recognize geography

insights.claim: The 1990s record cited includes direct U.S. intervention to stabilize Mexico’s financial system after the peso collapse, presented as a hard-nosed national-interest action rather than idealism.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Historical precedent for U.S. balance-of-payments rescue of a strategically important neighbor — relevant base case when handicapping U.S. response to a future Latin American financial crisis.
insights.quote: intervened to assist Mexico in righting its financial system after the collapse of the peso
insights.locator: We also passed the North American Free Trade Agreement
